correctness.rationale: The first-r winner remains at count r until T_{r+1}. Conditional hit probability is exactly 1/m, proving every k-indexed joint mass. Summing gives expectation difference. Independent Poisson clocks give exact gamma-tail integral. Uniform controlled small-time Laplace expansion gives two-scale rate. Poissonization, tightness and Riemann sums give the equilibrium-Weibull conditional law. The actual embedded rational and quadrature checks passed 165+12+6 assertions; these finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The question whether the earliest doubled birthday is also the earliest tripled birthday is a natural, marked dependence question not captured by waiting-time marginals. The exact all-multiplicity finite probability/time kernel, unusual persistence scale m^{-1/(r+1)}, and conditional equilibrium-versus-ordinary Weibull distinction yield a motivated structural answer rather than routine marginal recomputation.
